topic: WPI Base Year Revision and Introduction of PPI

subtopics.title: Wholesale Price Index (WPI) Basics
subtopics.summary: The Wholesale Price Index measures the average change in prices of goods traded at wholesale or producer level, before they reach final consumers. It is an important indicator of inflationary trends within the production and distribution chain. The Office of Economic Adviser compiles and releases it.
facts: Measures average change in prices of goods traded at wholesale or producer level
Captures prices before goods reach final consumers
Indicator of inflationary trends within the production and distribution chain
Compiled and released by the Office of Economic Adviser
Office of Economic Adviser works under the Department for Promotion of Industry and Internal Trade
Base year of the WPI before revision: 2011-12

subtopics.title: Base Year Revision and Major Reforms
subtopics.summary: The Government of India has approved revising the WPI base year from 2011-12 to 2022-23. The revised series changes the number of items, moves energy commodities to a different category, adopts a new weighting method and a new treatment of missing data. These changes aim to reflect the producer side of the economy more accurately.
facts: Government of India approved revision of WPI base year from 2011-12 to 2022-23
Number of items rises from 697 (WPI 2011-12) to 957 (WPI 2022-23)
Renewable energy inclusion adds Solar Power, Wind Energy and Nuclear Electricity as new components
Crude Petroleum and Natural Gas shifted from Primary Articles to Fuel and Power category
Revised weights are derived directly from Gross Value of Output
Earlier weights were based on Net Traded Value: Gross Value of Output + Imports - Exports
New missing-data approach: Targeted Mean Imputation
Previous missing-data approach: Carry-Forward Method, where missing prices were replaced by the last available price

subtopics.title: Producer Price Indices (PPIs)
subtopics.summary: For the first time, India will release dedicated Producer Price Indices with 2022-23 as base year. These indices track prices from the producer side and cover goods as well as services. Three indices are described: Output, Input and Service PPI.
facts: For the first time, dedicated PPIs will be released with 2022-23 as base year
Output PPI measures prices received by producers for goods and services they sell
Output PPI captures prices at factory gate or producer level, before taxes, trade margins and transportation costs
Output PPI reflects producer earnings and is an early indicator of future inflationary pressures
Input PPI measures prices paid by producers for inputs such as raw materials, intermediate goods and energy
Input PPI tracks production cost pressures and supply-side inflation
Service PPI measures prices received by service providers for services rendered
Services covered: banking, securities transactions, insurance, pension fund management, railways, air passenger transport and telecommunications

subtopics.title: WPI and PPI Compared
subtopics.summary: The PPI differs from the WPI in scope, focus, perspective and purpose. The WPI is primarily about goods and market-level wholesale prices, while the PPI covers goods and services and looks at producer revenue and input costs. The new PPIs are introduced alongside the revised WPI series.
facts: WPI scope: primarily goods; PPI scope: goods and services
WPI focus: wholesale price movements; PPI focus: producer-level price changes
WPI perspective: market-level wholesale prices; PPI perspective: producer revenue and input costs
WPI purpose: inflation monitoring; PPI purpose: comprehensive producer inflation analysis
New PPIs are introduced alongside the revised WPI series
Service PPI captures inflation trends in the services sector from the producer perspective

quizzes.passage:
Governments and analysts track changes in prices through a set of official price indices. The index known as WPI is treated as an important indicator of inflationary trends in the economy, and it is followed closely because it reflects price movements early in the chain of production and sale.

The Government of India has now approved a revision of the base year of this index. Along with the revised series, the government will introduce new indices for the first time. These are designed to give a more comprehensive assessment of inflation and cost pressures faced by businesses, so that pressures affecting firms are visible alongside those affecting buyers.

The index is built on the prices of goods that move between businesses and traders in large quantities. Its figures are published on a regular basis and help reveal how costs are changing across the supply network. The revision also updates the methodology, including the weights used, the treatment of missing price data, and the classification of certain commodities.

The aim of these changes is to make the index a more reliable guide to how sellers experience price movements. The revised structure is meant to reflect the present economy more accurately than the earlier series did.

IV. Chain whose inflation trends the WPI indicates   ->   D. Wholesale Price Index
At which level of trade are the WPI's goods priced?

Assertion (A): The WPI is an indicator of inflationary trends within the production and distribution chain.
Reason (R): The WPI measures retail prices paid by final consumers.

Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false

quizzes.passage:
Official price data help a country see how costs are moving through its economy. One important measure is an index that follows prices at an early point in the flow of goods, before the items reach ordinary buyers. Economists watch it closely because it reflects pressures that may later show up in shops and household budgets.

The government has approved a revision of the base year of this index. Along with the revised series, the government will introduce new indices for the first time. These are meant to give a broader view of price changes faced by firms that sell goods and services, including the costs they pay for inputs.

The revision also changes several technical features. The weights that give each item its importance are being rebuilt, and the method used to fill gaps in missing price data is being replaced. Some commodities are moving to different categories so that the classification reflects their role in the economy more accurately.

Taken together, the changes aim to make the index a more accurate guide to the production side of the economy, while keeping its place as a measure of price changes across the supply chain. Readers comparing the old and new figures will need to keep these differences in mind.

quizzes.passage:
Price data in India are released through more than one index, and two of them are compared on four features: scope, focus, perspective and purpose. A feature table is a useful way to read such comparisons, because it places the two measures side by side and shows where they differ.

The Government of India has approved a revision of the base year of one index, moving it to a newer reference period. Changing the base year is a technical step, but it affects how the index is read over time, so readers who compare old and new figures should keep the change in mind.

Each index has its own design, and the feature table shows how the two differ. The table has four rows, one for each feature, and two columns, one for each measure.

Because each measure has its own design, the two should not be treated as interchangeable. A reader who checks the table can see exactly where they differ and which question each measure is built to answer. The comparison discussed here is the feature table in the booklet's current affairs summary for June 2026.

quizzes.passage:
Indian price data come from more than one index, and two measures that appear together in recent reform discussions can be compared across four features. A feature table is a helpful way to read such comparisons, since it places each measure side by side and makes differences easier to see. The table has four rows, one for each feature, and two columns, one for each measure.

The four features are scope, focus, perspective and purpose. Scope refers to what the measure covers, focus refers to the kind of price movement it follows, perspective refers to the vantage point from which prices are viewed, and purpose refers to the question the measure is designed to answer.

The Government of India has approved a revision of the base year of one of these indices. Changing the base year is a technical step, but readers who compare old and new figures should keep it in mind. The revised series is to be released along with new measures that give a fuller view of price changes faced by businesses.

Because each measure has its own design, the two should not be treated as interchangeable. A reader who checks the feature table can see where they differ and which question each measure is built to answer. The comparison is taken from the booklet's current affairs summary for June 2026.
